name: – Niclas Herbst – § 1 – Am 53
title: REPORT on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the European Union for the financial year 2023, Section III – Commission, executive agencies and the ninth, tenth and eleventh European Development Funds
part_text: 1. Underlines its strong commitment to the Union’s fundamental values and principles which are enshrined in the Treaty on the European Union (TEU) and the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU); in the framework of the discharge process, stresses especially the principles of sound financial management as set out in Article 317 TFEU and the combatting of fraud and protection of the financial interests of the Union as set out in Article 325 TFEU; deplores the fact that, contrary to the stated values and very purpose of the founding of the Union, the European Commission is regularly the subject of scandals through its Commissioners or their close advisors: - alleged money laundering via lottery tickets by the Commissioner for Justice (potentially 1 million euros involved), the European Commission's inexplicable leniency towards its Director-General for Transport, who allegedly accepted free flights from Qatar airways, inexcusable decision by the Commission to pay a seven-year leave of absence with a total salary of 1.5 million euros for one of its directors accused of rape, without any attempt to recover the funds after the final conviction, case of pantouflage in a gas company of an adviser to the Vice-President of the Commission responsible for the environment and the Green Deal; - and through its operation: scandal of the administration of the Trust Fund for Africa denounced by the European Court of Auditors, scandal of the financing of NGOs by the European Commission with public funds to help it adopt a pseudo-climatic legislative package (Green Deal) via lobbying actions, financing of NGOs close to terrorist or Islamist movements;
